summary: The Anglican Church in North America's catechism, To Be a Christian, teaches that Jesus will return in victory, with great glory and power seen by all, to bring this age to an end, and that God will usher in a fully renewed creation. No one can know when he will return. All people, living and dead, will be judged by Christ: those apart from Christ will receive eternal rejection and punishment in hell, and those in Christ eternal blessing and the fullness of life with God. When he returns he will raise all the dead to bodily life. The catechism does not address purification after death.

points.question: What happens when Christ returns?
points.answer: His coming in glory and power will be seen by all people and will bring this age to an end; God will usher in a fully renewed creation. He will raise all the dead to bodily life and judge the living and the dead. No one can know when he will return.

points.question: What is the final state of the wicked?
points.answer: Those apart from Christ will receive eternal rejection and punishment in hell, while those in Christ receive eternal blessing and welcome into the fullness of life with God.
